question: Keď vyjdete z tunela Branisko rovno do ostrého slnka, nemalá časť ľudí neovládateľne urobí jednu vec. Ktorú?
source_excerpt: Photic sneeze reflex spurs light-induced sneezes in 10 to 30 percent of people.

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak driver knows the Branisko tunnel, and many have sneezed on leaving it without knowing why. The player assumes sneezing is caused only by dust or a cold. Learning that light alone triggers it in a large share of people is a 'so that's why!' moment, and the pack's theme gives a fair path to the answer.
extra.verification_notes: Photic sneeze reflex (ACHOO syndrome) makes an estimated 10-35% of people sneeze involuntarily when moving from dark to bright light (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/does-the-sun-make-you-sneeze).

explanation: Je to fotický kýchací reflex, ktorý má zhruba pätina až tretina ľudí. Vedci predpokladajú, že prudké svetlo podráždi aj nerv, ktorý spúšťa kýchanie.

question: Zívanie je nákazlivé – keď zíva jeden, čoskoro zívajú aj ostatní. Ktoré domáce zviera sa podľa vedeckých pokusov dokáže zívaním „nakaziť“ od človeka?
source_excerpt: 21 of 29 dogs yawned after seeing the yawn, while none yawned after the control movements.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone knows yawning spreads between people. Few people know it crosses species to the family pet, and more strongly with the dog's own owner. The player can work it out by asking which pet watches people most closely, and the explanation ends with a heart-warming twist.
extra.verification_notes: Dogs yawned in response to human yawns in the 2008 Joly-Mascheroni study (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2610100), and no newer finding contradicts it.

explanation: V pokusoch psy začali zívať, keď videli zívať človeka, a častejšie to bolo pri ich vlastnom pánovi než pri cudzom človeku.
